class.name: NetwSyncModel
class.brief_description: The declaration table that tells both peers which property set a wire ordinal names.
class.description:
An ordinal is the whole address a sync frame carries, so the two peers have to derive the same one from facts they both hold. That is why [method declare] assigns ordinals by SORTING a route's declarations rather than by the order they arrived: registration order is a function of tree entry, which two peers have no reason to agree on, and a set that registered second on one of them would otherwise decode as its sibling. The sort key is [member NetwSyncSetRow.kind], [member NetwSyncSetRow.key] and [member NetwSyncSetRow.record], and it admits no ties, because those three are exactly what makes a declaration distinct inside a route. Kind leads, so every [constant KIND_CONSUMED] row holds a lower ordinal than every [constant KIND_DERIVED] one. Ordinals are assigned once per declaration change and never during a pump, so a frame built in one pump and read in the next still addresses the row it was built for. [codeblock] # at registration, once var ordinal := model.declare( route, NetwSyncModel.KIND_DERIVED, key, comp, set.rid, set.record, set.wire_hash(), set.policy, set.audience)
# per pass, addressing by the ordinal alone var row := model.row(route, ordinal) [/codeblock]

method.name: attach
method.description: Remembers the object a declaration belongs to, so a frame that resolved its row can reach what feeds it without the caller scanning its own list. The attachment is keyed by the row's STABLE identity ([param kind], [param key], [param record]) and never by its ordinal, because [method declare] re-sorts a route and an ordinal moves. That is what lets [method binding_of] stay correct across a declaration the caller did not make. A null [param binding] detaches, which is the same act as [method detach] and is here so a caller re-attaching in a loop needs no branch.

method.name: authors
method.description: Whether the peer named by [param local_id] may author the row's stream this pass: the node authority for a row policed by the authority, the entity controller for a row policed by the controller, any peer for an open row. A state row is ALWAYS server-authored whatever its policy says, because it sits inside the rewind boundary: it feeds the server-authoritative state timeline, and entity control stamps the controller's authority onto the body, so following node authority would hand the state stream to the controlling client. A broadcast row is outside that boundary, a stream trusted outright, so it falls to its policy. [param node_authority] is the declaring node's own multiplayer authority verdict and [param controller] the entity's controlling peer, both facts the caller holds and this model does not. An [param ordinal] naming no row on [param route] authors nothing, because a row nothing can address is a row no frame can carry.

method.name: admits_schema
method.description: Whether the row's own [member NetwSyncSetRow.schema_hash] agrees with what the sender declared for that ordinal in [method note_descriptors]. An ordinal nobody declared a descriptor for is ADMITTED, which is the lazy-validation stance the consumed lane takes: a peer that never heard the spawn frame's descriptor section has nothing to disagree with. A declared descriptor that disagrees is refused, so two peers whose declarations differ drop the stream rather than misread it.

method.name: admits_sender
method.description: Whether [param sender] may write the row on this peer. The receive-side mirror of [method authors], validated against the receiver's own declaration rather than against anything the frame carried. The server is always trusted. A state row accepts the server ALONE, mirroring the send gate, so a controller-stamped node authority never smuggles client-authored state in. Every other row falls to [method NetwEntityControl.policy_admits] over its own policy. An [param ordinal] naming no row on [param route] admits nobody.

method.name: clear
method.description: Forgets every route's declarations and noted descriptors.

method.name: clear_route
method.description: Forgets [param route]'s declarations and its noted descriptors, which is what a route's death owes: a row that outlived its route would answer for an ordinal the next route assigns to something else.

method.name: binding_of
method.description: What [method attach] left for the row [param ordinal] currently names, or [code]null[/code] where the ordinal names no row or nothing was attached to it. This is the receive lane's whole lookup: a frame carries an ordinal and needs the thing that decodes it.

method.name: declare
method.description: Declares or replaces one row and answers its assigned [member NetwSyncSetRow.ordinal], or [code]-1[/code] where the declaration names no [param route] or no [param key]. Declaring re-sorts the route, so an ordinal read before this call may name a different row after it. A declaration that already exists under the same [param kind], [param key] and [param record] is UPDATED rather than added, so re-registering a node that re-entered the tree does not mint a second row for it. [param policy] and [param audience] are the gate columns [member NetwSyncSetRow.policy] and [member NetwSyncSetRow.audience] answer with. They default to the authority policy and the public audience, which is what a [constant KIND_CONSUMED] row carries: a consumed synchronizer has no set of its own to resolve them from.

method.name: detach
method.description: Forgets a row's attachment and LEAVES the row, because a declaration outliving the object that fed it is an ordinary state and not an error.

method.name: drop
method.description: Removes one row and closes the ordinal gap it left, so the route's ordinals stay a dense run. A route with no rows left is forgotten rather than kept empty.

method.name: event_recipients
method.description: Who an ON-DEMAND entity event reaches: a single property sync or signal, which no declaration row addresses and which therefore cannot go through [method recipients]. A host fans out to every peer of [param live], minus [param exclude]. A client sends to the server alone, because a client's event is a request the server relays. [param exclude] is the peer an event is being relayed FROM, so a sender never receives its own event back; pass [code]0[/code] when originating rather than relaying. It lives here beside [method recipients] because one class answering "who receives" for both lanes is what stops the two rules drifting apart, and the on-demand lane has no row of its own to hang the answer on.

method.name: note_descriptors
method.description: Records what the SENDER declared for [param route], as [param noted] mapping an ordinal to a schema hash, decoded from the spawn frame's descriptor section. [method admits_schema] validates arriving frames against it lazily, one row at a time, because a receiver may not have declared its own rows yet when the spawn frame lands. An empty [param noted] forgets the route's descriptors rather than recording an empty set, so an absent declaration and a declaration of nothing are the same thing.

method.name: recipients
method.description: Who the row's frames are for this pass. A server-only row reaches the server alone, and nothing at all when the server itself is [param local_id]. A public row reaches every peer of [param live], the peers the entity is currently live for, minus the local author. [param live] is passed in rather than looked up, because which peers an entity is live for is the liveness core's answer and not this model's. An [param ordinal] naming no row on [param route] reaches nobody.

method.name: route_rows
method.description: Every row declared on [param route], in ordinal order. Empty where the route has none.

method.name: route_bindings
method.description: Every attachment on [param route] of one [param kind], in ORDINAL order, which is wire order. A row with nothing attached is skipped rather than answered as null, so the result is what a caller can actually iterate.

method.name: row
method.description: The row [param ordinal] names on [param route], which is how a received frame resolves what it is addressing. Answers [code]null[/code] rather than a neighbour where the ordinal is outside the route.

method.name: row_for
method.description: The row a declaration names, which is how a sender finds the ordinal it was assigned. Answers [code]null[/code] where nothing was declared under that triple.

constants.constant: A synchronizer the kit consumed. Every consumed row precedes every derived one in ordinal order.
A property set derived from a script's own declarations.
